subtopic: Object Detection Anchors and Non-Maximum Suppression (NMS)
question_text: [Computer Vision & Feature Extraction - Q14] What is the mathematical criterion used by Non-Maximum Suppression (NMS) to eliminate redundant overlapping bounding boxes around a detected object?

options.text: Mean Squared Error of box centers
Intersection over Union (IoU) exceeding a specified threshold (e.g. 0.5) against the highest-scoring candidate box
Cosine distance between bounding box aspect ratios

answer_explanation: NMS greedily selects the box with the highest confidence score, then discards any remaining candidate box whose Intersection over Union (IoU) with that top box exceeds the suppression threshold.
reference_solution: Correct Choice: B. Rationale: NMS greedily selects the box with the highest confidence score, then discards any remaining candidate box whose Intersection over Union (IoU) with that top box exceeds the suppression threshold.

criteria.name: Correctness
criteria.description: Selects the exact correct technical option.
